title: Hardware lane zoning and noisy-worker dampening for dedicated GPU pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a zoning and mitigation subsystem for Dedicated GPU pools to provide hard throughput guarantees while reducing noisy-worker impact. This ticket defines a pragmatic implementation that combines hardware lane zoning (explicit assignment of racks/hosts to customer slices), per-slice token leases for throughput guarantees, and a lightweight noisy-worker dampening layer that detects and attenuates pathological workloads without full eviction. The feature must integrate with autoscaling controllers, the quota reconciliation service, and the Console alerting dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Customers with reserved capacity observe no more than 10% throughput regression during noisy neighbor incidents compared to baseline SLA tests
Autoscaler respects slice token leases and will not downscale reserved lanes below guaranteed throughput targets
Noisy-worker dampening reduces tail-latency P99 spikes by at least 30% in synthetic multi-tenant injection tests
Quota reconciler can surface per-slice overuse events in Console with links to remediation playbooks
Rolling upgrade path exists: feature can be toggled per-cluster via runtime feature flag with zero downtime for active requests
implementation_notes: Zone model: small fixed number of zones per region (3–7) mapped to rack groups; each Dedicated customer can be assigned one or more zones for hard separation
Token leases: a bucket of throughput tokens issued per-zone per-customer refreshed every second; tokens consumed by the scheduler to admit requests into the fast-path

Dampening: lightweight local controller samples request characteristics (latency, memory amplification, KV-cache churn). When a worker exceeds configurable anomaly thresholds, dampening reduces admit rate and applies progressive backpressure to new requests from offending sessions
Fallbacks: when zone capacity exhausted, requests can be routed to a lower-cost shared pool with explicit degradation messages returned to SDKs via structured response codes
Metrics: add per-zone per-customer gauges for tokens issued/used, dampening events, eviction_score, and admission_reject_count
tradeoffs: Hard zoning improves isolation but reduces packing efficiency; our token lease approach tries to reclaim idle tokens via short-term borrowing with conservative hedging
Dampening avoids aggressive eviction (better customer experience) but may allow some degraded latency — acceptance criteria bound acceptable degradation
Implementation complexity: scheduler changes are invasive; split into incremental PRs starting with read-only telemetry and opt-in zone assignment
test_plan: Unit tests for token lease accounting and token refill logic
Integration test: multi-tenant harness that runs synthetic LLM workloads to validate throughput SLAs under injected noisy clients
Chaos test: randomly crash nodes inside a zone and verify autoscaler maintains throughput by moving spare capacity (respecting leases)
Performance benchmark: compare P50/P95/P99 for reserved vs shared pools before and after dampening enabled
End-to-end canary: enable on a non-critical region for 2 weeks and validate Console metrics and alerts
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): opt-in zone assignment + telemetry only in region us-west-2 (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (limited customers): enable token leases and dampening for 5 pilot Dedicated customers; monitor SLIs and customer feedback (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): allow zone assignment for new Dedicated customers and provide migration playbook for existing ones (6 weeks)
Phase 4 (GA): enable self-serve zone selection in Console and promote feature flag to default
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly conservative token hedging leaves capacity unused — Mitigation: telemetry-driven tuning and short-term borrowing mechanism with global safety limit
Risk: Dampening misclassifies high-variance but legitimate workloads — Mitigation: whitelist heuristics for known workloads and human-in-the-loop override via Console
Risk: Scheduler regression affecting latency — Mitigation: staged rollout with benchmark gates and automatic rollback if P99 degrades beyond threshold
Risk: Increased operational surface (more metrics) — Mitigation: dashboard templates and alert-runbooks added to runbook repo
